bibl.title: Loose Bonds and Porous Boundaries among Mobile People as Religious Agents in the Greco-Roman Arabian Desert.
bibl.seg: Anna-Katharina Rieger, Loose Bonds and Porous Boundaries among Mobile People as Religious Agents in the Greco-Roman Arabian Desert.
Religion in the Roman Empire 3 (2017) pp. 11-49, figg.
bibl.note: 1. Coincidental groups, virtual networks and conceptual spaces: 1.1. Material practices of groups and constraints of the archaeological record; - 1.2. Places of repetitive and multicultural religious activity in the Arabian Desert. - 2. Different options at Wadi Ramm [Southern Jordan]: 2.1. Groupings of images and texts at the spring; - 2.2. Groupings of images and texts at the temple; - 2.3. Who and where? Differences in dedicational practices between spring and temple. - 3. From ephemerality to recurrence: concentration of religious activities at so-called Paneia in the Arabian Desert of Egypt: 3.1 Space- and time-spanning networks? Intra-site group styles at el-Kanayis; - 3.2. Intra- and inter-site relations at Wadi Ḥammāmāt. - 4. Conclusion: Ephemeral groups, loose bonds and porous boundaries in road-side sacred places.
